annotation.title_clean: Automation hits the knowledge worker: ChatGPT and the future of work
annotation.title_en: Automation hits the knowledge worker: ChatGPT and the future of work
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Berg, J.; Gmyrek, P. (International Labour Office)
annotation.venue: ILO Voices - The Future of Work Podcast (ILO Research Brief)
annotation.summary_en: ILO policy brief on the impact of LLMs such as ChatGPT on knowledge workers. It argues task transformation is likelier than mass job loss, stresses job quality alongside quantity, highlights precarious data-labelling work, and urges social dialogue and occupational safety and health regulation. No embodied AI content.
key_provisions_or_claims: Knowledge work covers 644-997 million jobs globally (19.6-30.4% of employment).
LLMs more likely to transform tasks than eliminate jobs outright.
Job quality matters alongside job quantity; effects depend on how transitions are managed.
Data-labelling 'invisible workers' face precarity and psychosocial risks, needing OSH systems and regulation.
Social dialogue should be used early when designing and adopting technological systems.
